clue.text: Storm all but hurtled around prison

indicators.note: around says the shortened word wraps itself about the next piece
all but says the word for hurtled is used minus its final letter

parts.note: to hurtle is to rush, so hurtled means hurried
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A storm almost sent someone flying round a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm with very strong winds.

clue.text: Riding a horse in short bursts?

definitions.meaning: ... is riding a horse at an ordinary pace, often a hired one
a ... cough comes in short dry bursts

explanation.surface: A rider goes out on horseback in fits and starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacking is both going out on a horse for a ride and coughing in short harsh spasms.

clue.text: All are drunk with English beer

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Everyone gets drunk on English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are drunk' scrambles ALLARE to REALAL; E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is cask-conditioned beer, the traditional British kind.

clue.text: Botanist leaves, having gathered agave fibre

indicators.note: having gathered means the two words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A botanist departs after collecting plant fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the botanist's foliage; it only gives letters to the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a coarse fibre from Mexican agave plants, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Circus acts are unusual — one's bringing in the top people

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of are come out in an odd order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is one is
the A-lists are the most famous people

explanation.surface: Circus performances are rare, and someone is bringing in the celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns ARE into AER. 'acts' means performers here, as in a circus line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerialists are trapeze and high-wire performers, typical circus turns.

clue.text: Italian poet, losing head, getting upset — a source of disturbance in Italy

definitions.text: a source of disturbance in Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Dante is the great Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian poet loses his head and gets angry, troubling Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts DANTE to ANTE; 'getting upset' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna, the active volcano in Sicily, causes eruptions and earthquakes.

clue.text: Student no longer in thrall to enthusiast

parts.note: L is the learner plate, a crossword stand-in for a student
to be over someone or something is to have got past being captivated by them

explanation.surface: A student has fallen out of love with a former passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover of something, like a music lover, is a keen fan of it.

clue.text: Biblical tribe and Biblical prophet heading off Biblical monster

parts.note: Levi was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: Nathan is the prophet who rebuked King David

explanation.surface: A tribe and a prophet face down a monster, all from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' cuts NATHAN to ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviathan is the huge sea creature described in the Book of Job.

clue.text: Sedative mercenary carried around Romania

indicators.note: carried around means the word for mercenary holds the next letters inside

parts.note: venal means mercenary, open to bribes
RO is the international code for Romania

explanation.surface: A hired soldier carted a sleeping drug round Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mercenary' looks like a noun for a hired soldier; here it is an adjective meaning open to bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronal was an early barbiturate drug used to induce sleep.

clue.text: Begrudge losing second railway, putting in again?

indicators.note: losing means the letter for second is removed from the word

parts.note: to resent is to begrudge

explanation.surface: Someone resents losing a second railway, wanting it put back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes S from RESENT, leaving REENT. The question mark marks the loose definition: a re-entry is a putting in again.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is going or being put back in, like a spacecraft returning to the atmosphere.

clue.text: Branch of society unfavourable about Knight — here's the evidence

parts.note: a chapter is a local branch of a society or club

indicators.note: about says the word for unfavourable is wrapped round the letter for knight

parts.note: adverse conditions are unfavourable ones
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A local branch of a club speaks against a knight, and here is the proof.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting N inside ADVERSE after its first A gives ANDVERSE, read as AND VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give chapter and verse is to cite exact sources, the precise proof for a claim.

clue.text: Distribution of aid taking years, sadly? It wouldn't surprise me

indicators.note: distribution spreads things about, so the letters of aid are rearranged
sadly, as in badly or poorly done, says the letters of years are jumbled

explanation.surface: Aid handed out takes years, which is no shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution of' turns AID into IDA and 'sadly' turns YEARS into RESAY; 'taking' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: I dare say is a phrase admitting something is likely, so its being true would be no shock.

clue.text: Revoking barrel regulation will bear fruit

indicators.note: revoking turns back a decision, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: Cancelling a rule about barrels will pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revoking' reverses TUNLAW. 'will bear' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A walnut is the edible nut of the walnut tree, a botanical fruit.

clue.text: British overlooking rail network? It's accommodating many

parts.note: transport that ignores the railway relies on roads, so it is road-based

explanation.surface: A British view over the railway network suits a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' seems to mean looking down on; it means ignoring, so transport overlooking rail is ROAD-BASED. 'It's' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-based movement or coalition draws in a wide range of people.

clue.text: Soldier about to enter Reading after riot

indicators.note: to enter says the short word goes into the middle of the jumbled town name
after a riot a place is in disorder, so the letters of Reading are scrambled

parts.note: re is Latin for about, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to march into the town of Reading after a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after riot' scrambles the town's letters to GNADIER, with the short word slotted in after the G. Reading is a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades, now a guards regiment member.

clue.text: Attacking the man, representing him a demon

indicators.note: representing means the letters are re-presented in another form

explanation.surface: An attack portrays a man as a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad hominem argument targets the person instead of their reasoning; Latin for 'to the person'.

clue.text: Completely eradicating foremost seasonal plant

indicators.note: eradicating the foremost letter means the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: wholly means completely

explanation.surface: A seasonal plant is being wiped out entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly, with its red berries, is the classic Christmas decoration plant.

clue.text: Rich husband setting limits to one's fidelity

indicators.note: setting limits on both sides means the outer letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: rich food is fat
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is one is

explanation.surface: A wealthy husband puts bounds on a person's loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting limits to' puts FATH round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith in the sense of good faith means loyalty and keeping one's word.

clue.text: Ball carried by soccer team employed in targeted manner

definitions.note: the participle focused is read as describing how something was done

indicators.note: carried by means the letter goes inside the team's abbreviation

parts.note: FC is Football Club
the letter O is shaped like a ball
used means employed

explanation.surface: A soccer team carried the ball and used it precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' puts O inside FC. The definition reads as 'used in a focused way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A focused effort is aimed tightly at one goal, just as a targeted one is.

clue.text: Fierce changes involving climate, ultimately — how's the Arctic in summer?

indicators.note: involving means the jumble wraps round the extra letter
changes means the letters of fierce are rearranged
ultimately picks the final letter of climate

explanation.surface: Fierce climate change is making the Arctic summer different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' scrambles FIERCE to ICEFRE and 'involving' puts climate's last letter E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: With global warming the Arctic sea loses its ice in summer, so it is clear of ice.

clue.text: A lot to teach boy about love

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them

indicators.note: about means the word for boy wraps round the letter for love

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone is to teach a boy all about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside LAD to make LOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainload is as much as a train can carry, a large quantity.

clue.text: Origin of outcry supported by Times over a former acid compound

indicators.note: in a down clue being supported means sitting on top of the next piece
in a down clue over means the next letters sit above the rest
origin is the starting point, so the first letter of outcry is taken

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
late means former, as in the late president

explanation.surface: An outcry backed by The Times about something past turns into a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the X of multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxalate is a salt or ester of oxalic acid, found in rhubarb leaves.

clue.text: Opening secured by the German fishing-boat

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the article that follows

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a rift is a crack or opening

explanation.surface: A gap is plugged by the German trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing boat that uses drift nets.

clue.text: Concern expressed with a later surprised comment? That's rich

indicators.note: later says the letter a is moved to a place further on in the word

parts.note: care means concern or worry
my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone voices worry, then later adds an astonished remark about wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' moves the A of the word for concern to its end. 'expressed' and 'That's' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich food is full of cream or butter, so creamy is a fair synonym.

clue.text: A friend with a lot of regular business in Arab city

parts.note: bud is American slang for buddy, a friend

indicators.note: a lot of but not all means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a habit is something done regularly

explanation.surface: A friend does a great deal of routine trade in an Arab city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes HABIT without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Dirty work that has to be done to protect Society

indicators.note: to protect means the word for obligatory work surrounds the letter for society

parts.words: work that has to be done
parts.note: a duty is a task you are obliged to do

explanation.surface: Grubby jobs must be done to keep society safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts S inside DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty things are covered in dust and so unclean.

clue.text: Determination to see power slipping from grasp with time

indicators.note: slipping from means one letter leaves the word and another takes its place

parts.note: a grip is a grasp
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Resolve sees strength escape from one's hold over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping from' takes P out of GRIP and 'with' brings in T.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, the will to keep going.

clue.text: Not suffering with repeated washing, but avoiding psychological interpretation?

definitions.meaning: describes fabric that does not get smaller when washed
a shrink is a slang word for a psychiatrist, so resisting one is avoiding being analysed

explanation.surface: A fabric that survives the wash, but also a patient dodging analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into SHRINK, slang for a psychiatrist, and RESISTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink-resistant cloth keeps its size after laundering; the joke reading is someone fending off a psychiatrist.

clue.text: Engineers engaged in major engineering project showing vision

indicators.note: engaged in means the letters for engineers go inside the next word

parts.note: a dam is a big civil engineering project
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers working on a vast building scheme show foresight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream, like a vision, is an image seen in the mind or an ambition.

clue.text: Toy top's initial whirling motion to endure

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of the word top's

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl of water or air
to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: A spinning top's first spin is a toy that must keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft toy shaped like a bear.
